summary: The household is one person, age 80 and disabled, with gross income of about $2,539 a month. In Jan–Feb 2026 that is above Arizona's 185% FPL expanded categorical eligibility limit, so the regular rules apply, and the net income and asset tests both deny benefits ($0). From March 2026 Arizona's limit is 200% FPL ($2,608.33 a month; $2,660 from October). The USDA BBCE table, updated 2026-06-29 (before the freeze), confirms 200% with no asset limit. That makes the household categorically eligible, which waives the income and resource tests. 7 U.S.C. 2017(a) and 7 CFR 273.10(e)(2)(ii)(C) then give the $24 FY2026 minimum benefit to every eligible one-person household, even though the benefit formula is negative. The engine's 10 × $24 = $240 matches this. Using $24 for Oct–Dec is right because the FY2027 COLA came out after the freeze. The $0 consensus applies 185% or the regular rules for the whole year.
